notes: The plan's Batch 4 bar: gain >= 10% of the ENCLOSING OPERATION, or >= 50 ms per drag frame. Under = DROP, not merge.
Every number here is on the owner's real design, never the committed 400x400 clip (gate rule 2).
Call counts are recorded beside every clock (gate rule 3): three of the seven registers described a mechanism the count contradicted.

M-10's register entry says `_orient_downhill` samples the DEM twice per diversion drawn. The count says a draw makes 38 full-band reads: `_overflow_options` calls `_feature_elevation` once per OTHER earthwork, so a 35-feature design reads the band 34 extra times before the properties dialog can appear.

M-12's register entry says ~250 full-raster passes per full analysis on 5 spillways. The design has 29 sited spillways, but `_isolated_burn` is handed no sills, so the per-feature capacity pass reaches `_cut_spillway` 32 times for 0.1 ms total. The double rasterise IS real in the burn (`_bar_cells` n=58 for 29 notches, exactly 2x), it is simply not worth 10%.
R-5's register entry says a shared pool pays per member. The count says 43 (barrier, pool) pairs over 39 distinct pools, so memoising by pool removes 9% of the function, not most of it.

G-8's register entry says rasterio `shapes()` traces every zero region of a 2.85 M-cell array. Measured: passing `mask=` saves 2.2 ms of a 22.0 ms polygonise. The premise is right and the cost is not there.

Out of scope but recorded: `find_ridgelines` returns 0 lines on this design. All 1462 skeleton components are shorter than `min_cells` (50 cells at 1 m). The Ridgelines button spends 5.8 s to produce nothing.
Out of scope but recorded: `_on_spillway_placed` costs 4.6 s and `_on_vertex_edit_finished` 5.6 s on this design. Neither is in this plan.
M-6's precedent stands: a measured number decides, and the owner may merge under the bar with the number in hand (M-6 merged at 8.0%).
AFTER, same probes, same design: M-11 5835.4 -> 85.4 ms; the Keypoint run 6075.6 -> 342.7 ms. Q-11 18.4 -> 5.2 ms per tick. G-9 18.2 -> 0.3 ms to arm a tool. M-10 989.9 -> 345.6 ms to the dialog.

M-11 find_ridgelines.operation: Keypoint analysis run: DrainageLineAnalysis() + find_keypoints + find_ridgelines
M-11 find_ridgelines.mechanism: 1462 skeleton components, every one of them below min_cells=50; the loop pays a full-raster `labeled == region_id` + argwhere for each. Loop as written 5701.2 ms; bincount + find_objects equivalent 8.9 ms.

Q-11 dam dialog band read.operation: _update_capacity(), the dialog's whole response to one spin-box tick
Q-11 dam dialog band read.per_frame_verdict: 15.3 ms against the 50 ms drag-frame bar: under it, but a spin tick is not a drag frame and the share bar is the one that applies
Q-11 dam dialog band read.mechanism: src.read(1).astype('float32') on 1139x1016 to sample ~60 cells, per tick, on the GUI thread inside a modal

G-9 draw tools slope band.operation: activate_draw_line(): construct the tool after a toolbar press
G-9 draw tools slope band.mechanism: full slope band read in DrawLineTool.__init__, and a fresh tool is built per draw action

M-10 snap_point_to_contour_elevation.operation: _on_geometry_drawn up to dlg.exec(): draw a feature and wait for the properties dialog
M-10 snap_point_to_contour_elevation.mechanism: 38 full-band reads per draw (38 rasterio.open, all of them this function); 15.0 ms each saved by a 1x1 window
M-10 snap_point_to_contour_elevation.denominator_note: Pricing it against `_orient_downhill` gives 83.5% and is meaningless — `_orient_downhill` is made of the two samples. That is gate rule 1's own trap and was rejected.

M-12 _cut_spillway.operation: burn_earthworks (8016.6 ms) + the per-feature terrain-capacity pass (11462.7 ms)
M-12 _cut_spillway.mechanism: _cut_spillway n=35, _bar_cells n=58 (exactly 2x per notch, as the register says), _downhill_step n=29. In the capacity pass: _cut_spillway n=32 for 0.1 ms, because _isolated_burn passes no sills.
M-12 _cut_spillway.verdict_note: Removing ALL of _cut_spillway cannot reach 10% of either operation. Settled without coding it, per gate rule 1.

R-5 overtopping_spill.operation: a Verify run (run_with_earthworks end to end)
R-5 overtopping_spill.mechanism: 29 barriers, 43 (barrier, pool) pairs, 39 distinct pools. Memoising the pool work removes 9% of the function, so the real gain is ~83 ms = 0.4% of a Verify run.
R-5 overtopping_spill.verdict_note: Two independent reasons to drop: the ceiling is under the bar, and the mechanism the register priced barely occurs on a real design.

G-8 ponding query polygonise.mechanism: 310 ponds, largest 1840 cells. _mask_to_qgs_geometry 22.0 ms; with mask= 19.8 ms; geometry identical.

M-11 find_ridgelines.note: the per-component loop that cost 5801.2 ms re-measured at 8.9 ms as bincount + find_objects; 68x on the function, 17.7x on the Keypoint analysis run

G-9 draw tools slope band.was: 18.2 ms to arm a draw tool
G-9 draw tools slope band.note: 60x; the band is read once per terrain instead of once per tool

M-10 snap_point_to_contour_elevation.was: 989.9 ms from finishing a line to the dialog
M-10 snap_point_to_contour_elevation.note: the function itself 16.2 -> 2.6 ms; _orient_downhill 33.0 -> 3.1 ms (two points, one open). What is left is 36 opens at ~2.2 ms each plus the dialog's own construction.
